explanation: Swiss designers Max Miedinger and Eduard Hoffmann first called it Neue Haas Grotesk. It was renamed in 1960 to sell better abroad.

claims.text: The name Helvetica comes from Helvetia, the Latin name for Switzerland.
Helvetica is not named after Hungary, the Netherlands or Belgium.
Helvetica was designed in 1957 by Max Miedinger with Eduard Hoffmann of the Haas Type Foundry in Switzerland.
The typeface was released as Neue Haas Grotesk and renamed Helvetica in 1960.
